root_cause.text: The `last_gc` timestamp in `nf_conncount` was updated unconditionally on every new connection addition instead of only when garbage collection (GC) actually occurred, allowing a high packet rate to keep `last_gc` recent and bypass GC, causing unbounded list growth.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "Currently last_gc is being updated everytime a new connection is tracked, that means that it is updated even if a GC wasn't performed. With a sufficiently high packet rate, it is possible to always bypass the GC, causing the list to grow infinitely." The patch removes the unconditional update of `list->last_gc` after adding a new node and adds it earlier in the function at a point where GC (removal of an old connection) has just been performed (after `nf_ct_put`), ensuring that `last_gc` is only refreshed when GC actually happens.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the last garbage collection timestamp after processing a found connection to ensure proper GC timing.
intent_record.what: Added assignment `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` after the if block that calls `nf_ct_put(found_ct);`.
intent_record.how: This sets the `last_gc` field of the list structure to the current jiffies timestamp, ensuring that the last garbage collection time is updated after each processed found connection.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect update of last_gc timestamp on connection insertion, ensuring it is only updated by the garbage collection routine itself.
intent_record.what: Removed the assignment of `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` from the `__nf_conncount_add` function, which previously updated the last garbage collection timestamp every time a new connection was added to the list.
intent_record.how: After removing this line, `list->last_gc` is no longer overwritten with the current jiffies upon adding a new connection. This preserves the previous `last_gc` value (likely set during actual garbage collection), thereby altering the behavior of any garbage collection logic that relies on this timestamp.
